sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
No drag & drop. Let me think about this from a completely different angle.
Maybe the two panels at the bottom are actually "level info": the left panel (plus shape with dots) and the right panel (checkerboard) might be decorative "logo" elements that appear in every level. In that case, the actual puzzle is: S-block + neck + bar + tail.
What's the relationship between the S-block and the tail? The S-block has a b frame and an S core. The tail has a b half and an S half. The tail is a "miniature version" of the S-block! The S-block is a 5×5 (frame + core), the tail is a 4×4 (two halves).
Maybe the goal is: the tail is a "key" that should be inserted into the S-block's frame? The S-block's frame is at columns 12-16, the tail's minimum column is 23. They can't touch.
Or the goal might be: the tail should be at the right end (initial position) and the S-block should...
Hmm, wait. Maybe I have it backwards: the S-block is the "player" and the tail is a "goal/target" that the player has to reach? But the arrow keys move the tail, not the S-block.
Let me test: press UP multiple times — does the S-block move? No, in the earlier UP the tail rotated.
Hmm, what if the arrow keys move both the S-block and the tail? Let me check: in the initial state the S-block is at (17-22, 12-16). Currently also at (17-22, 12-16). It has never moved. So no.
What if the tail is a "cursor" that selects a slot, and the S-block moves to the selected slot?? The S-block has never moved.
OK, another thought: what if the goal involves the timer? Like, "stop the timer at the right moment"? What does the timer do? It's growing (white from the top). When it fills up... game over? Or level clear?
Actually, wait. What if the white bar is the level's progress, and it increases when you perform "correct" actions? Let me compare: white increased during LEFT moves (5, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16), UP (7), DOWN (8), RIGHT (9), UP (18), DOWN (20), LEFT (23), LEFT (24)... but it didn't increase on MOUSE clicks or on the first LEFT (1, 4). Actually, it increased on almost every action that changed the board. So it's simply time-based.
Let me check the actual timing: I'll measure white's height and the step count right now. If it's time-based, it should keep growing even without actions. I'll wait a few seconds (just call python twice with a sleep in between? Can't sleep... actually, I can import time and sleep in python! The tool runs my code; time.sleep(3) should work).
Let me test: read white's height, sleep 5 seconds, read again. If it grows without actions → time-based timer.
And the goal might be: make the timer stop (by completing the puzzle), or the timer is a countdown to game over.
Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Maybe this is a "Simon"-style pattern game: the S-block blinks and you have to repeat it? No, there's no animation.
Or maybe the goal is simply: move the tail to the leftmost slot, rotate it so the S half faces left (toward the S-block), and... the S half is S-colored, same as the S-block's core. If the S half faces left, it's "connecting" the S-block and the bar? Currently b faces left. To make S face left: the tail needs to be horizontal with S on the left, b on the right. How? Move RIGHT (b faces right, S faces left) — but that also moves the tail to the right. Then the tail is at columns 27-30 with S on the left (27-28), b on the right (29-30). The S half faces left, toward the S-block! And it's at slot 2 (not the leftmost).
Hmm, so the configuration "S half facing left toward the S-block" can be achieved at any slot by moving RIGHT from the slot to its left.
Is that the goal? "Align the S half with the S-block's direction"? But the S half is at columns 27-28, the S-block is at 13-16, separated by the neck. The neck is at rows 19-20; the tail's S half (horizontal orientation) is at rows 19-22, and its top 2 rows (19-20) align with the neck! So S-block (13-16) - neck (17-22) - S half (27-28)?? No, there's a gap at 23-26 (the b half is at 29-30... wait, if the tail is at 27-30: S is 27-28, b is 29-30; the gap between the neck (ending at 22) and the S half (starting at 27) is 23-26 — not connected.
If the tail is at the leftmost (23-26) with S on the left: S is 23-24, b is 25-26. Then S-block (13-16) - neck (17-22) - S half (23-24) - b half (25-26). Connected chain! S-block → neck → S half → b half. A complete "S chain"!
How to get the tail to the leftmost with S on the left: from the leftmost, press... LEFT at the leftmost rotates. Current state: leftmost, b on the left (S on the right). Press LEFT → rotates clockwise? Earlier: S on top → (LEFT) → b on left. So the rotation direction: S top → S right? No wait: before that LEFT, the tail was S on top (S at rows 19-20, b at rows 21-22). After that LEFT: b on left (columns 23-24), S on right (columns 25-26). So the S half moved from top → right. That's a clockwise rotation.
So LEFT at the boundary rotates clockwise: S top → S right → S bottom → S left → S top...
Current: S right. Press LEFT → S bottom. LEFT → S left. There it is: the tail is at the leftmost with S on the left, b on the right!
Then the chain: S-block - neck - S half - b half.
Is that the goal? Maybe. Or maybe after that, press LEFT again (S left, b right — b faces right, away from the S-block)...
Let me try it: LEFT, LEFT to get S on the left, observe. Then maybe click the S-block, or press LEFT again.

Plan: press LEFT twice (S-right → S-bottom → S-left), observe; then test further LEFT/click.
